title: Variant Traffic Playbook — Quickstart snapshot assets for canary, A/B, fallback
creator: Lena Ortiz
description: Deliver a compact, developer-focused quickstart asset bundle demonstrating how to use variant traffic controls (canary, A/B, and fallback policies) from the Console. Assets should be optimized for docs and in-product help: annotated screenshots, compact mobile/responsive variants, a single-page playbook image (artboard) and 2 short looping GIFs that show traffic percentage changes and automatic fallback. Include callouts for: where to pin a model version, how to configure a canary window, A/B weight controls, and how fallback routing triggers. Provide recommended copy snippets for the docs team and short keyboard-copyable CLI commands to match UI actions.
acceptance_criteria: Single-page playbook artboard (1440px) with numbered callouts for 7 key steps and microcopy approved by PM
Three annotated screenshots for desktop: Traffic table, Variant config modal, Fallback policy modal (each exported as 2x PNG)
Two responsive variants for mobile (375px width) showing collapsed variant list and quick-action menu
Two looping GIFs (~6s) demonstrating: (1) increasing canary from 0% to 20% and (2) automatic fallback when primary model fails
Assets uploaded to Drive and linked in PR; docs PR merged with inline images and alt text
Accessibility checklist completed: text contrast, alt text for images, captions for GIFs
Designer and PM sign-off recorded in ticket comments
comments: 2026-03-02 — Lena Ortiz: Initial brief uploaded to Confluence. PM asked for a single-page 'playbook' to live at the top of the rollout docs; keeping it lightweight for copy-and-paste usage.
2026-03-04 — Mateo Chen: Early sketches in Figma shared. Chose a compact 7-step flow to avoid duplicating existing rollout visuals. Decision: show both UI and CLI toggle examples side-by-side.
2026-03-06 — Product review (Aakash Patel): Prefer emphasizing 'fallback triggers' with a red microcopy state. Also requested a micro-interaction mock for the automatic fallback path.
2026-03-07 — Design review (Nora Kim): Reviewed GIFs; recommended slower easing for the canary percentage animation to make change readable. Noted margin adjustments for mobile screenshots.
2026-03-08 — Accessibility review (Samira Khan): Suggested alt text templates and caption text for GIFs. Confirmed contrast ratios for badges.
2026-03-09 — Mateo Chen: Uploaded exports to Drive and opened docs PR. Pending QA to verify copy matches console labels exactly.
2026-03-10 — Lena Ortiz: PM approval received in thread. Next: finalize localized strings for EN/ES/DE and handoff to engineering for in-app help tooltip insertion.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: GIFs are slightly larger to preserve clarity; we agreed to limit to two GIFs to minimize page weight
Tradeoff: Chose compact artboard over full tutorial flow to reduce maintenance burden when Console UI iterates frequently
Decision: Use real console screenshots with anonymized data rather than illustrations to keep developer trust high
